item.title: Tate and Artin--Tate Motivic Tensor-Triangular Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.40806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the Balmer spectra of geometric Tate and Artin--Tate motives with $\mathbb{F}_p$-coefficients over any field whose characteristic differs from $p$. For Tate motives, we find the bigraded comparison map to be a homeomorphism to the homogeneous spectrum of the motivic cohomology of the base field. For Artin--Tate motives, we describe the spectrum as a gluing of the spectrum of Artin motives computed by Balmer--Gallauer with the punctured Tate spectrum. We determine all specialisations between these pieces and the resulting topology. Under the hypothesis that the spectrum of rational Tate motives is a singleton, we also compute the integral Tate spectrum after inverting the exponential characteristic of the base field. As a consequence of our results, we identify the punctured Tate spectrum as an open subspace of the spectrum of the category of geometric Voevodsky motives, and draw some conclusions concerning the latter. Finally, we include an appendix where we define generalised periodicity in the context of tensor-triangular geometry, and explore its applications in motivic settings.
item.dc:creator: Jean Paul Schemeil, Fraser Sparks

item.title: Integral Hodge structures and atoms of fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.40811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following the recent work by OpenAI on the irrationality of very general cubic fourfolds in Hassett divisors, we prove some compatibility of Iritani's blow-up formula with the classical blow-up decomposition of integral Hodge structures. As a consequence, we express OpenAI's birational invariant in terms of the theory of atoms developped by Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu. We also show that, for every smooth complex rational cubic fourfold, the primitive cohomology is isometric as an integral Hodge structure to the twisted middle cohomology of a K3 surface and we prove irrationality of the very general Verra fourfold.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emy Gu\'er\'e

item.title: Truncated Grassmannians: polytopes, representations, and Cauchy formulas
item.description: arXiv:2610.40891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this paper is to develop algebraic and combinatorial techniques for studying the geometric properties of truncated Grassmannians, a class of algebraic varieties obtained via certain projections of classical Grassmannians within their Pl\"ucker embeddings. We introduce a class of cyclic representations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of the general linear Lie algebra, which are proved to serve as duals of the homogeneous components of coordinate rings of truncated Grassmannians. We prove that the characters of these representations are computed via truncated Cauchy formulas and establish a connection with coordinate rings of complete collineations. We also construct monomial bases of these representations in terms of certain generalized chain polytopes and use the RSK correspondence to establish connections with Cauchy-type formulas and with Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Feigin, Igor Makhlin

item.title: Uniformization of compact K\"ahler Threefolds of Zero Kodaira Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.40950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given two smooth compact K\"ahler threefolds $X$ and $Y$ whose universal covers are biholomorphic, we show that $\kappa(X) = 0$ if and only if $\kappa(Y) =0$.
item.dc:creator: Anna Choblet

item.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bryan, Oberdieck, Pandharipande and Yin predicted the number of hyperelliptic curves on general abelian surfaces under a transversality condition. Some of the numbers have already been confirmed. In this paper we construct singular hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ polarised abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$ confirming a few predicted numbers, namely of (geometric) genus $g=d$ and of geometric genus $k+3$ on $(1,2k)$ and $(1,2k+1)$ polarised surfaces. Moreover, we have found that all genus 7 hyperelliptic curves on general $(1,8)$ polarised surfaces are double coverings of curves locally embedded into $(1,4)$ polarised surfaces. More interestingly, there is a unique genus 9 hyperelliptic curve (up to translation) locally embedded into a general $(1,12)$ polarised surface and it is a Klein covering of a curve locally embedded into a $(1,3)$ polarised surface.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Bor\'owka, Paolo Grossi, Anatoli Shatsila

item.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
item.description: arXiv:2610.41031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $\kappa$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tilde{\Delta}$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--G\"ottsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}|$ of $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Tangi Pasquer

item.title: An atomic approach to Shokurov's conic-bundle conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.41174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we apply a weaker version of Hodge atoms to show that a standard conic bundle over a smooth complex projective rational surface $S$ is irrational if $|2K_S+\Delta|\ne\emptyset$, where $\Delta$ is the discriminant divisor. This proves Shokurov's conjecture on rationality of conic bundle threefolds. As an application, we deduce precisely which nodal quartic double solids are rational.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Ludmil Katzarkov, Daniel Pomerleano, Zhijia Zhang

item.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.41237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$. The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $\iota_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincar\'e duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.
item.dc:creator: Kiwamu Watanabe

item.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.41287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(\mu)$ associated to a partition $\mu=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \kappa_\mu:=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]
item.dc:creator: Scott Mullane

item.title: Disconnectedness of stability manifolds and their geometric loci, and separation of braid orbits of semiorthogonal decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proves that the Bridgeland stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ has infinitely many connected components for general quintic threefolds, other general complete intersection Calabi--Yau threefolds, certain odd-dimensional Calabi--Yau varieties, and certain rational weak Fano varieties. Moreover, we show that the geometric locus $\mathrm{Stab}^{\mathrm{geo}}(X)$ meets distinct connected components of $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ for general quintic threefolds and their products with varieties with finite Albanese morphisms, which gives examples in any dimension at least three. For the weak Fano examples, we also construct semiorthogonal decompositions in infinitely many braid group orbits. The proof is an extension of Nordskova's argument to families, using semilinear autoequivalences and absolute Galois actions on geometric generic fibers to permute mutually orthogonal spherical objects. Then, we specialize the separation to closed fibers. In our examples, the spherical objects are constructed from rigid rational curves or spinor bundles on quadrics.
item.dc:creator: Genki Ouchi, Tomoki Yoshida

item.title: Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.41578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $\Gamma$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.
item.dc:creator: Jen-Chieh Hsiao

item.title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.41587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.
item.dc:creator: Jen-Chieh Hsiao

item.title: Relative Du Bois complexes over higher dimensional bases
item.description: arXiv:2610.41719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the notion of the right relative Du Bois complex to a smooth base of arbitrary dimension. We further show that this complex satisfies base change in the sense of Kov\'acs--Taji, for flat families with strict higher Du Bois fibers, extending the result by Ning over a smooth curve.
item.dc:creator: Dora Kassabova, Haoming Ning

item.title: Deformations of Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.41727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work of Brantner and Taelman shows that derived deformation theory and period maps can recover strong mixed-characteristic lifting results. In this paper, we develop a prismatic version of this method for Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms, constructing compatible deformations over $A/I^n$ for every $n$ under suitable hypotheses. We also apply our method to $F$-split Calabi--Yau varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. In particular, we consider an $F$-split smooth proper variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$, with $H^{d-1}(X,O_X)=0$ and trivial canonical bundle. We show that $X$ admits a lift to $W_3(k)$.
item.dc:creator: Tingxiao Shi

item.title: $K$-tropical curves, Riemann-Roch and Serre duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.41737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We endow a tropical curve with the structure of a ringed space and establish analogues of Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for these ringed spaces. As a corollary, we give a cohomological proof of the tropical Riemann-Roch theorem.
item.dc:creator: Soham Karwa, Joseph Rabinoff

item.title: A Tropical Viewpoint on the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.41931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a tropical perspective on the recent arguments announced by OpenAI for Nagata's conjecture and the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture. By degenerating to both the normal cone and a semistable model whose dual graph is a cycle, we replace sections on a surface by Laurent polynomials in two variables. In place of theta functions, tropical methods bound the exponents of these Laurent polynomials, and a lift of the tropical Abel--Jacobi class of the normal bundle controls the shape of the resulting exponent diagram. Combining these support bounds with interpolation on a torus proves the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture with its predicted threshold whenever the corresponding linear series contains an integral curve whose only singularity is an ordinary node that is not a basepoint.
item.dc:creator: Juliette Bruce

item.title: The metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4
item.description: arXiv:2610.41954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a counterexample to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4. Here, we prove that the metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture is true in dimension 4. More precisely, let $f,g\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be germs of reduced holomorphic functions, and let $\varphi\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism such that $\varphi(V(f))=V(g)$. We prove that if every irreducible component of the tangent cone of $V(f)$ at the origin has a singular locus of dimension at most two, then $V(f)$ and $V(g)$ have the same multiplicity at the origin. In particular, the multiplicity of complex analytic hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\leq 4$, is an embedded bi-Lipschitz invariant; the cases $n=2$ and $n=3$ were known. This extends a previous result of the author for tangent cones whose components have singular loci of dimension at most one. We also prove that two irreducible homogeneous hypersurfaces whose singular loci have dimension at most two, and which are mapped onto each other by a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{C}^n$ fixing the origin, have the same degree.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio

item.title: Motivic invariants of birational hyper-K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.42045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that birational projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds have equivalent integral cohomological motives as commutative algebra objects in $\mathrm{SH}(\mathbb C)$. Consequently, their algebraic K-theory spectra are equivalent as $E_\infty$-algebras, and their integral graded K-theory rings are isomorphic.
item.dc:creator: Weimufei Wu

item.title: Grassmannians of absolute Banach-Colmez Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.42110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Grassmannians of absolute Banach--Colmez spaces and prove the $k$-Grassmannian is perfectoid if and only if the space has slope $< 1/k$. For $d=1$, this proves a conjecture of Hansen--Mann. The key ingredient is a Pl\"{u}cker morphism, which realizes the $k$-Grassmannian of a slope $d/n$ space as a Zariski closed subspace of the projectivization of a slope $kd/n$ space. We also introduce a general method to construct invariant elements in perfectoid Tate--Huber pairs, and use this to prove absolute Banach--Colmez spaces of slope $<1$ have perfectoid projectivizations. As applications, we establish vanishing bounds for Scholze's mod $p$ Jacquet--Langlands functor on parabolic inductions, and also prove its vanishing in the top degree on every infinite-dimensional non-supersingular irreducible representation.
item.dc:creator: Zecheng Yi

item.title: Abelianization and moment maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.42123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$. We do this by looking at the restriction of $\mu$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.
item.dc:creator: Elana Kalashnikov, Ruxandra Moraru, Francisco Villacis

item.title: Weighted flip graphs from cyclic quantum mutations: pentagon inequalities and exponential separations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Positive cyclic quantum mutations at a third root of unity induce an explicit weight on polygon flip graphs. We study the resulting discrepancy between minimum flip count and minimum accumulated normalization loss. Every pentagon three-to-two replacement strictly decreases weight, and in connected types $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$ every minimum-weight path is a flip geodesic. In type $A_4$, however, a six-flip path has smaller weight than the unique five-flip geodesic. A compatible positive projective gluing construction amplifies this example to an exponential success-probability separation in every connected type $A_n$, $n\ge4$. We also give a quantitative perturbation bound preserving the separation. The low-rank minimality statement has an exhaustive finite certificate; the pentagon inequality and the all-rank construction are analytic. In the associated sequential postselection model, differences of path weights determine success-probability ratios independently of the input state. The comparison holds for separately normalized exact mutation steps.
item.dc:creator: Xiaomin Tang

item.title: On Boundary State Screening via Solitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.40777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a coarse classification scheme for the boundary data of massive QFTs based on transitions of boundary states via soliton / kink profiles. Starting from the lattice of boundary states, we introduce the boundary screening group $\mathbb{B}$: the equivalence classes of boundary states which cannot be connected by such transitions. In string theory backgrounds which geometrically engineer an interacting QFT in the target space, $\mathbb{B}$ computes the worldsheet analog of the target space defect group $\mathbb{D}$. When $\mathbb{B}$ is non-zero, it provides a diagnostic for having a target space with non-normalizable modes. For interfaces between QFTs, similar considerations imply the existence of a non-trivial conserved charge associated with soliton absorption / transmission, which means that the interface cannot fully dissolve / disappear. Similar considerations hold for junctions of QFTs, which in the special case of string worldsheet CFTs translate to junctions of string theories. We illustrate these general considerations with a number of non-geometric 2D $\mathcal{N} = (2,2)$ Landau-Ginzburg models, as well as their natural lifts to 4D $\mathcal{N} = 1$ Wess-Zumino models.
item.dc:creator: Vivek Chakrabhavi, Babak Haghighat, Jonathan J. Heckman

item.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
item.description: arXiv:2610.40815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Alessandr\`i, Jiazhi He

item.title: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.41573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Th\'el\`ene, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Gambardella, Nguyen Manh Linh

item.title: Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.41631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.
item.dc:creator: Ronnie Cheng

item.title: Alcove walks, crystal structure and a Levi branching rule
item.description: arXiv:2610.41929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the Borel case $P=B$, we endow Haines' set of maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks (arXiv:2405.17174) with a crystal structure. We construct a bijection with the LS-gallery model of Gaussent and Littelmann (arXiv:math/0307122) and prove that it intertwines the root operators. This answers a question raised by Haines. We also extend the Gaussent-Littelmann stratification to the parabolic setting, prove the Levi branching rule for LS galleries, and compare the resulting gallery model with Haines' maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks in the parabolic setting.
item.dc:creator: Wenzhuo Wang

item.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.42022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.
item.dc:creator: Yassine El Kaouni

item.title: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.42134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As observed by Kienzle and the second author, rank-two $\mathcal{O}(3)$-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encode all hyperbolic crystals of genus two: the spectral curves are the unit cells, and the Hitchin fibers are the abelian Brillouin zones. In a uniform magnetic field of two flux quanta, the lowest Landau level is one-dimensional at every nonzero momentum, and, as found by Iengo and Li, its dimension jumps to two at the zero momentum. We identify the states of the lowest Landau level with the Baker--Akhiezer sections of the Higgs bundles, and their zeros, the vortices, with the Baker--Akhiezer divisors. A family of nonzero momenta limits to the zero momentum exactly when each of the two vortices approaches the image of the other under the spatial inversion, and the states of the jumped level are labeled by the directions of limiting. On the Higgs bundle side, the zero momentum is the point where the Hitchin fiber intersects the Hitchin section. Such a family of Higgs bundles limits to the Hitchin section, thereby crossing to a lower stratum of the \BB stratification, an example of the phenomenon investigated in terms of Baker--Akhiezer divisors by the first author with Figiel and Teschner.
item.dc:creator: Duong Dinh, Steven Rayan

item.title: The Fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra over nontrivially valued fields and the radius of convergence of nonarchimedean differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2303.12124v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a fundamental theorem for tropical partial differential equations, analogous to the fundamental theorem of tropical geometry in this context. We extend results from Aroca et al., Falkensteiner et al. and from Fink and Toghani for the case of trivial valuation as introduced by Grigoriev to differential equations with power series coefficients over any valued field. Crucial ingredients are the framework for tropical partial differential equations introduced by Giansiracusa and Mereta and a result on infinite intersections of projections of fibers of tropicalizations, which we prove using Hrushovski and Loeser's model-theoretic interpretation of Berkovich analytification. As a corollary of the fundamental theorem, we show that the radius of convergence of solutions of an ordinary differential equation over a nontrivially valued field can be computed tropically.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Gallinaro, Stefano Mereta

item.title: Characteristic polynomials and eigenvalues of tensors
item.description: arXiv:2308.10957v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We lay the geometric foundations for the study of the characteristic polynomial of tensors. For symmetric tensors of order $d \geq 3$ and dimension $2$, and symmetric tensors of order $3$ and dimension $3$, we prove that only finitely many tensors share any given characteristic polynomial, unlike the case of symmetric matrices and the case of non-symmetric tensors. We propose precise conjectures for the dimension of the variety of tensors sharing the same characteristic polynomial, in the symmetric and non-symmetric settings.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Galuppi, Fulvio Gesmundo, Ettore Teixeira Turatti, Lorenzo Venturello

item.title: Birational geometry of log Calabi-Yau pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3, D)$ of coregularity 2
item.description: arXiv:2402.13970v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper aims to study the birational geometry of log Calabi-Yau pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3, D)$ of coregularity 2, where in this case $D$ is an irreducible normal quartic surface with canonical singularities. We completely classify which toric weighted blowups of a point will initiate a volume preserving Sarkisov link starting with this pair. Depending on the type of singularity, our results point out that some of these weights do not work generically for a general member of the corresponding coarse moduli space of quartics.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Alves da Silva

item.title: Turning non-smooth points into rational points
item.description: arXiv:2402.14969v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a recent paper, the author and St\"ohr established a bound on the number of iterated Frobenius pullbacks needed to transform a non-smooth purely inseparable point on a regular geometrically integral curve into a rational point. In this paper we improve this result, by establishing a new bound that is sharp in every characteristic $p>0$.
item.dc:creator: Cesar Hilario

item.title: Asymptotic geometry of non-abelian Hodge theory and Riemann--Hilbert correspondence, rank three $\widetilde{E}_6$ case
item.description: arXiv:2407.20638v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Geometric P=W conjecture in rank 3 on the three-punctured sphere. We describe the topology at infinity of the related character variety. We use asymptotic abelianization of harmonic bundles away from the ramification divisor and an equivariant approach near the branch points to find the WKB (also known as Liouville--Green or phase-integral) expansion of the involved maps. We analyze the Stokes phenomenon governing their behavior.
item.dc:creator: Miklos Eper, Szilard Szabo

item.title: Algebraic tori in the complement of quartic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2411.03506v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $B\subset \mathbb{P}^3$ be an slc quartic surface. The existence of an embedding $\mathbb{G}_m^3\hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^3\setminus B$ implies that $B$ has coregularity zero. In this article, we initiate the classification of coregularity zero slc quartic surfaces $B\subset \mathbb{P}^3$ for which $\mathbb{P}^3\setminus B$ contains an algebraic torus $\mathbb{G}_m^3$, and equivalently, the classification of cluster type pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3,B)$. Along the way, we give criteria for a log Calabi--Yau pair $(X,B)$ over a toric variety $T$ to be of cluster type.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of the London Mathematical Society, 113(1):e70427, 2026
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Alves da Silva, Fernando Figueroa, Joaqu\'in Moraga

item.title: Constructing and transforming standard resolutions of local modules
item.description: arXiv:2508.11306v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct standard resolutions for analytic local modules on complex hypersurfaces using standard basis methods, with extensions to complete intersections. The algebraic version over arbitrary infinite fields is also suggested. Applications include derived category formula of local hypersurface blow-ups, revealing new connections between standard bases and categorical geometry.
item.dc:creator: Xingbang Hao

item.title: Degeneration of Derived Quot schemes, Lagrangian Foliations, and categorical Donaldson-Thomas invariants
item.description: arXiv:2510.20325v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a derived-geometric framework for Donaldson--Thomas invariants in semistable Calabi--Yau threefold degenerations. Derived restriction from the two smooth components of the central fiber to their common anticanonical divisor is Lagrangian. We give explicit universal-family diagrams for this structure, compare the deformation complexes with perfect complexes on the singular union, and construct the fourfold duality using a canonical bundle pulled back from the base. On specified Quot presentations we describe the real Lagrangian foliation and its shifted potential. We formulate proper-completion and cohomological-comparison conjectures for sheaves arising from sections of an extending line bundle. Their specialization is described by oriented two-sided bar complexes and a finite Gauss--Manin system.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Kryczka, Artan Sheshmani

item.title: On the tensor-triangular geometry of isotropic motives
item.description: arXiv:2511.05922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the tensor-triangular geometry of the categories of isotropic Tate motives, isotropic Artin motives and isotropic Artin--Tate motives. In particular, we study the categories $DTM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$, $DAM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$ and $DATM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$ where $k$ is a flexible field and we fix $\mathbb{F}_2$-coefficients. In this case, we prove their Balmer spectra are singletons. The proof of this relies on the fact that the categories in question are generated by objects whose morphisms are `nilpotent enough.' Furthermore, we investigate their homological spectra, and verify Balmer's Nerves of Steel conjecture in these cases by showing these spaces are also singletons, and we give an explicit description of the homological primes. We also investigate stratification, and we conclude by studying generation properties of these categories -- the latter results we see also apply to global (i.e. non-isotropic) motives.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Sparks, F. (2026), On the tensor-triangular geometry of isotropic motives. J. London Math. Soc., 114: e70752
item.dc:creator: Fraser Sparks

item.title: On the Jacobian algebras of Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2604.25637v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a Ziegler pair of plane arrangements, that is two plane arrangements $\mathcal{A}:f=0$ and $\mathcal{A}':f'=0$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^3$, such that the intersection lattices $L(\mathcal{A})$ and $L(\mathcal{A}')$ are isomorphic, but the Betti numbers of the minimal resolutions of their Jacobian algebras are not the same. We introduce several properties for such pairs and relate them to cones over Ziegler pairs of line arrangements in $\mathbb{P}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Dimca, Piotr Pokora

item.title: A stacky resolution of singularities for orders by Azumaya algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.05137v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a stacky resolution of singularities for certain noncommutative spaces which can be viewed as 'finite noncommutative extensions' of schemes. More precisely, we show that any order over a reduced separated finite type scheme over a field of characteristic zero can be resolved by an Azumaya algebra over a smooth Deligne--Mumford stack by a sequence of stacky blow-ups.
item.dc:creator: Timothy De Deyn

item.title: Disconnected Stab(X) and infinitely many braid group orbits
item.description: arXiv:2607.25391v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions Stab(Y) on a very general quintic threefold Y has infinitely many connected components. Using similar methods, we also prove that for a particular smooth projective (weak Fano) threefold X the braid group action on the set of full exceptional collections in Dscr^b(X) has infinitely many orbits, in particular, it is not transitive. This provides a counterexample to a conjecture of Bondal and Polishchuk from 1993. The conjecture was first disproved by Chang, Haiden, and Schroll, who constructed a family of partially wrapped Fukaya categories for which the transitivity fails. However, no counterexample of the form Dscr^b(X) for X a smooth projective variety was previously known. In addition, we show that Stab(X) also has infinitely many connected components. These are the first known examples of a smooth projective varieties whose spaces of Bridgeland stability conditions are disconnected.
item.dc:creator: Anya Nordskova

item.title: Jordan-H\"older theory for complementary polyhedra and moduli of parahoric Higgs torsors
item.description: arXiv:2609.17231v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend Behrend's theory of complementary polyhedra to include Jordan-H\"older theory by introducing the notion of Jordan-H\"older facets. As a consequence, we can construct Jordan-H\"older parabolic subgroup schemes for reductive group schemes over a smooth projective curve. We use these results to provide a uniform approach to describing Jordan-H\"older filtrations and S-equivalence of moduli stacks of semistable bundles, including vector bundles, principal bundles, parabolic bundles, parahoric torsors, and parahoric Higgs torsors, following Zhang. We explicitly give a description of Jordan-H\"older filtrations and S-equivalence in the semistable locus of parahoric torsors and parahoric Higgs torsors, coming from their good moduli spaces, as constructed by Alper-Halpern-Leistner-Heinloth and R\'ega. This application uses the Rees construction, as given by Heinloth, to identify filtrations of moduli stacks of parahoric torsors with reductions of parahoric torsors to parabolic subgroups, inducing Jordan-H\"older stratifications of the moduli stacks.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Roth

item.title: A natural Chow lemma for smooth threefolds and fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.05427v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth proper integral variety of dimension at most four over a field of characteristic zero. We construct a finite sequence of blowups along smooth centers with projective endpoint, preserving the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective opens of $X$. The construction depends only on a fixed functorial principalization procedure and is natural under isomorphisms, including those over different ground fields. The proof has two parts. A colength argument on regular local surfaces gives, in every dimension, a finite preparation after which some maximal quasi-projective open has complement mapping into codimension at least three in $X$. In dimensions at most four these images are points or curves. Ample numerical classes on the normalized components of that complement give finite bounds for summing base ideals of linear systems. The resulting ideal descends to the original field; geometric integrality is not required.
item.dc:creator: Parsa Bakhtary

item.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16760v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Galois coinvariants of the geometric \'etale fundamental group and \'etale cohomology of varieties over a finitely generated field $k$. We establish finiteness properties of these coinvariants for (possibly infinite) Galois extensions $L/k$ such that $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As applications, we obtain finiteness results for $L$-rational torsion points on abelian varieties and \'etale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over number fields.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Steklov

item.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.19037v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,\Phi)$ corresponds to a representation $\rho$ of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$, then $(E,-\Phi)$ corresponds to $(\overline{\rho}^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $\eta\mapsto-\eta$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.
item.dc:creator: Krishnendu Gongopadhyay, Tathagata Nayak

item.title: The Yau Geometric Conjecture for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.24636v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a proof of the long-standing Yau Geometric Conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Fu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: On the existence of polarized varieties without weakly Ulrich bundles, ordinary instantons with bounded quantum number and supernatural bundles with bounded roots
item.description: arXiv:2610.36231v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an obstruction to the existence of bundles $\mathcal E$ on a smooth $n$-dimensional polarized variety such that $\mathcal E$ is $a$-regular and $\mathcal E^*(K_X+(n+1)H)$ is $b$-regular. In particular, this gives an obstruction to the existence of weakly Ulrich bundles. Using these obstructions and some recent examples of \cite{a1} in dimension $2$, we prove that for any $n \ge 2$ there exist many smooth $n$-dimensional varieties $X$ with a very ample line bundle $H$, such that there is no weakly Ulrich bundle for $(X,H)$, no ordinary instanton bundle with bounded quantum number, no non-ordinary $\mu$-semistable instanton bundle with bounded quantum number and no bundle with supernatural cohomology and bounded roots.
item.dc:creator: Ozhan Genc, Angelo Felice Lopez

item.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, remixed
item.description: arXiv:2509.00954v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For each endotrivial complex for a $p$-group arising from Bredon homology of a representation sphere, we construct $p$-local quasi-isomorphisms, called forerunners. These enable us to extend Balmer--Gallauer's results concerning the tensor-triangular geometry of permutation modules for elementary abelian $p$-groups to all $p$-groups. We construct an open cover of the Balmer spectrum under which all endotrivials are tt-line bundles, that is, every endotrivial is locally isomorphic to a shift of the tensor unit. We define a remixed permutation twisted cohomology ring for which the canonical comparison map from the Balmer spectrum to the homogeneous spectrum of the twisted cohomology ring is injective. If the twisted cohomology ring is Noetherian, the comparison map is an open immersion, and the open cover endows the Balmer spectrum with Dirac scheme structure. We prove Noetherianity holds for Dedekind groups and the dihedral group of order 8, and conjecture it holds for all $p$-groups.
item.dc:creator: Sam K. Miller

item.title: The variety of orthogonal frames
item.description: arXiv:2512.25058v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An orthogonal n-frame is an ordered set of n pairwise orthogonal vectors. The set of all orthogonal n-frames in a d-dimensional quadratic vector space is an algebraic variety V(d,n). In this paper, we investigate the singularities and components of the variety V(d,n), as well as the algebraic properties of the quadratic ideal I(d,n) generated by the orthogonality relations, which cuts out V(d,n) set-theoretically. By a general result of Ananyan and Hochster, these objects satisfy increasingly strong regularity conditions when d becomes large compared to n; we establish optimal effective bounds to quantify this behavior. We give criteria for the ideal I(d,n) to be prime or a complete intersection, thereby resolving open problems proposed by Conca and Welker. We give criteria for the variety V(d,n) to be normal or factorial. We provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture that I(d,n) defines V(d,n) scheme-theoretically. As applications, we improve the existing bounds for when the Lov\'asz-Saks-Schrijver ideals of simple graphs satisfy these four properties.
item.dc:creator: Laura Casabella, Alessio Sammartano

item.title: Index and Robustness of Mixed Equilibria: An Algebraic Approach
item.description: arXiv:2603.04298v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present two results regarding the relation of the index of equilibria and the index of fixed points, and the index of equilibria and payoff-robustness: any integer can be the index of an isolated completely mixed equilibrium of a finite game. In a particular class of isolated completely mixed equilibria, called monogenic, the index can be 0, +1 or -1 only. In this class non-zero index is equivalent to payoff-robustness. We also discuss extensions of the method of computation to extensive-form games, and cases where the equilibria might be located on the boundary of the strategy set. These results follow from a new method of computing indices of equilibria, which we also develop in this paper, that is based on algebraic properties of the system of polynomials describing completely mixed equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Pahl
